context_sources.name: Neumayer 2005, asylum migration to Western Europe
Fussell and Elliott 2014, demographic responses to disaster

limitations: The symbol table has its meanings detached from the symbols.
Weighted sums print with subscripts split onto adjacent lines.
The resource-update definition is repeated four times with the same symbol.
The transition matrix is printed with dots in place of most entries.
Table 7 has its columns shifted, and the summary totals are not reconciled with it.
GDP tables repeat countries and split names across rows.

tasks: Define metrics for the refugee crisis
Model the flow among origins and destinations
Allow the parameters to change over time
Set policy for health and safety
Add exogenous events such as war
Test the model at larger scale

section_map.summary: Four moves, 637000 a year, cap of 50187 a month.
Three weighted blocks, weights by assertion.
Faith gate, two mortalities, a sparse graph.
Capacity falls by arrivals, belief can reform.
Habit penalties and a hard law flag.
One war impact zeroes a route.
Stable below ten times, weaker at fifteen.
Inaccurate data, tangled diagrams, clustered scores.
Three advices: matching, a buffer zone, doctors.

contributions.summary: A three-block index whose weights are asserted and then narrated off a chart.
A faith gate that explains why the transfer graph is sparse.
A single war impact that zeroes a route and forces resettlement.

dependency_graph.handoff: The factor blocks decide which country traits enter the flow
The routed flows are what deplete resources and capacity
The updated faith flag and capacity feed the transition matrix
The transition weights are what get retested when the flow is scaled

assumptions.summary: Countries with few refugees can be ignored.
A difference of faith blocks the transfer entirely.
Wealth only falls during the journey.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Faith of each country tabulated and used as a zero-one flag.
GDP and population for the receiving countries.

models.summary: Three weighted blocks summed into one index.
A capped flow with a faith gate and two mortalities.
Resources and capacity depleted by arrivals.
A transition matrix with a war override.
Conflict rising with the excess over transport.

verification.summary: The dropped preparation time is added back and the ranking barely moves.
Stability read off a degree distribution at several scales.

results_trace.summary: 637000 a year across six routes, capped at 50187 a month.
Culture and faith dominate the computed transition matrix.
Stable below ten times the base scale, weaker at fifteen.

writing_logic.summary: Each factor is motivated by the failure it prevents, before the formula.
Adjectives such as most direct and most intense become the weights.
Policy is derived backward from a stated priority.

language_observations.summary: The summary is a numbered tour: first, second, third, finally.
The work section repeats the summary almost word for word.
A sparse graph is explained in one plain sentence.
The letter comes last and gives three advices, each tied to a result.

visualization_observations.summary: Table 1: symbol definitions, detached from their rows.
Figure 1: factor influence, read aloud in rank order.
Figures 2 to 5: parameter surfaces for resources, space and policy.
Table 7: transfer counts by origin and destination.
Figure 8: the transfer graph with more conditions.
Figures 9 and 10: parameters under exogenous events.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Every weight rests on accordance with the actual situation.
Religion is treated as a hard gate with no exception tested.
Stability is asserted from small changes without reported magnitudes.

weaknesses.summary: Data are not accurate enough, so results may be wrong.
At large scale the scores cluster and the ranking loses force.
The summary itself says accuracy needs improving.

independent_extensions.summary: Estimate the weights from data instead of asserting them.
Reconcile the route totals with the transfer table.
Model the pressure a host puts on its neighbors.

candidate_rule_impacts.summary: Derive the instruments backward from the stated priority.
Name the scale at which the model stops holding.

unresolved_questions.question: Do the six route totals add up to the table of flows?
Where do the weights 0.6, 0.8, 0.4, 0.3 and 0.2 come from?
Why does stability fail at fifteen times and not earlier?
